data.cause: The firewall's WAN NIC driver (vtnet0) has wedged: its TX queue keeps hitting watchdog timeouts so nothing leaves the box, which is why four successful DHCP/interface reloads never restored connectivity even though the cable modem re-registered and reports OPERATIONAL.
evidence: dmesg -a: repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP' cycles — the WAN queue stalls repeatedly.
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 -n 8.8.8.8: 'sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss — no traffic can be emitted on the WAN at all.

arp -a -n: next-hop 198.51.100.1 shows '(incomplete) ... expired' while the LAN host 10.20.0.9 resolves fine — ARP requests are not reaching the provider side, so the break is local to the firewall's WAN path, not a routing/NAT problem.
netstat -i: vtnet0 has 48211 output errors (Oerrs) versus 0 on the LAN interface, while ifconfig still reports vtnet0 'status: active' with lease address 198.51.100.27 intact.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json and events.jsonl: outage_start ~02:06, reloads at 02:30, 02:40, 02:55, 03:25 all returned rc=0 yet the outage persisted; at 03:30 the watchdog logged action 'none', reason 'reload_cap', reloads_24h 12 of max 12 — the auto-reload path is exhausted and ineffective because it does not reset the stuck driver.

modem-events.jsonl / modem-metrics.jsonl: modem event 90000000 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21 and cm_status OPERATIONAL with growing uptime (1620s -> 5280s) at every sample after 02:29 — the provider link itself recovered, so the remaining outage is on the firewall side.
data.recommendation: Reboot gw.lan (firewall_reboot) to reset the wedged vtnet0 driver — a WAN reload alone has already been tried four times with rc=0 and no recovery, so only a full host restart will re-initialize the NIC. The maintainer is away, so this needs to be run under the fallback rule rather than waiting for approval. Afterwards, verify that ping to 198.51.100.1 succeeds and the ARP entry for the next hop resolves; if the watchdog timeouts recur on the same queue, treat the virtio NIC as suspect hardware and replace/pass through it differently. Separately, have the watchdog escalate instead of silently hitting its 12-reload cap, and ask the ISP about the 02:01:44 'No Ranging Response - T3 time-out' and the modem's unexplained reboot, which started the incident but had already self-healed.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN transmit queue stall (watchdog timeouts)
